solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wretched fellow's a convict, with short time inside

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fellow, the 's being a link

indicators.note: the time is placed inside the word for the convict, cutting it open

parts.note: a lag is old British slang for a convict
a minute shortened to its abbreviation, min

explanation.surface: A grim picture of a wretched man in prison serving a brief stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flaming' is mild British slang used, like 'wretched', to vent annoyance. 'Lag' is old British slang for a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild British expletives of exasperation, as in 'that wretched dog' or 'that flaming dog'.

clue.text: Dandy's clothes extremely smart — they're of interest to snappy types?

definitions.text: they're of interest to snappy types?

indicators.note: used as a verb: the dandy's word dresses, or surrounds, the other letters

parts.note: a fop is a dandy; the possessive supplies the S

indicators.note: the extreme letters of the word smart, its first and last

explanation.surface: A fashion note: a dandy's wardrobe is extremely smart, of interest to snappy dressers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snappy types' are not sharp dressers but photographers, who snap pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Aperture settings on a camera lens are marked in these stops, which photographers care about.

clue.text: It involves moon, star and far side of galaxy

definitions.text: It involves moon, star and far side of galaxy

indicators.note: to involve is literally to roll up or entangle, so the two words are tangled into a new order
the far side of the word galaxy is its last letter

explanation.surface: A description of a science that deals with the moon, stars and galaxies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves' tangles MOON and STAR into ASTRONOM, and Y ends the word. The whole clue also describes the science itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The scientific study of celestial bodies covers the moon, stars and distant galaxies.

clue.text: Island with a touring business?

indicators.note: going round, so the island and the a travel around the word for business

parts.note: biz is informal shorthand for business, as in showbiz

explanation.surface: A description of a holiday island with a thriving tourist trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts I and A around BIZ. The whole clue also describes the Balearic island, famous for its tourism.
explanation.definitionFit: This Spanish Balearic island is a major tourist destination, so it is literally an island with a touring business.

clue.text: Soldier on with one European, going around south of Greece

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means placed below, so after

parts.note: GR is the abbreviation for Greece

indicators.note: turning round, so the three pieces are read backwards

parts.note: re means on, concerning
I is the Roman numeral one
a Dane is a European

explanation.surface: A soldier pressing on with a European comrade, travelling around southern Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier on' reads as one phrase, but 'Soldier' alone is the definition. 'going around' turns the pieces backwards into ENADIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier is a soldier, originally one who threw grenades, now a member of a guards regiment.

clue.text: US sportsman's agent retired when about to die

indicators.note: the turned agent goes about, or around, the word for longing
withdrawn, going back, so the word for agent is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent
to be dying to do something is to itch to do it

explanation.surface: A sporting agent, now retired, at the point of death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'die' here means long eagerly, as in 'dying to', not expire. 'retired' gives PER, which goes 'about' the longing.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball, the player who throws the ball to the batter is called this.

clue.text: Under pressure to go on for self- respect

indicators.note: in a down clue the riding piece sits under the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics
to ride is to go on a horse or vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone pressured to carry on for the sake of their dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: A sense of one's own worth and dignity is a synonym for this word.

clue.text: Cutting or ditch primarily attracts conservationists

parts.note: a trench is a ditch

indicators.note: first of all, so just the opening letter of attracts

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, the British conservation charity

explanation.surface: A digger's choice: cut a channel, or let a ditch draw the conservation lobby.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting remark is incisive and sharp, the same sense as this adjective.

clue.text: Male sheep pursues clipped female, getting agitated

indicators.note: follows, so the sheep comes after the other piece
cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: her is the female pronoun
a tup is a ram

explanation.surface: A ram chasing a shorn ewe, both getting worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipped' suits the sheep-shearing surface but is a trimming signal on the pronoun. A tup is a British dialect word for a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal phrase means worked up or anxious, matching agitated.

clue.text: Commonwealth Day, Irish Guards raised capital

indicators.note: lifted up, so in a down entry the letters read from bottom to top
the words guard, or hold within them, a run of letters

explanation.surface: A parade on Commonwealth Day with the Irish Guards raising a flag in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guards' keeps HDAYIR inside the words, and 'raised' reads it upwards. The Irish Guards are a British Army regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the seat of government of Saudi Arabia, so a national capital.

clue.text: Dress suit tailored principally for African

indicators.note: first of all, so just the opening letter of tailored
to dress is to arrange, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A dress suit cut chiefly for an African customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' rearranges SUIT plus T, the first letter of 'tailored'. 'Dress suit' reads as formal wear but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a people of Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa.

clue.text: Very gradually heading off, carrying explosive device

indicators.note: holding inside, so the trimmed word goes around the explosive
the head, or first letter, of the word is removed

parts.note: gently means gradually, as in a gently rising slope
a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: Someone slowly setting off while carrying a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops G from GENTLY to leave ENTLY, which, 'carrying' MINE, becomes E-MINE-NTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: This adverb means extremely or to a high degree, as in eminently sensible.

clue.text: Spread rumour of decent attendance at match?

indicators.note: a rumour is hearsay, so the sense is what is heard

parts.note: a proper gate: proper meaning decent, a gate being the crowd at a sports match

explanation.surface: Spreading gossip about a respectable crowd turning up for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport the gate is the number of spectators at a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread an idea or a plant is to multiply or disseminate it, the same verb sense.

clue.text: Could odd characters secure relationship with his help?

definitions.text: Could odd characters secure relationship with his help?

indicators.note: to hold fast, so the odd letters hold the ratio inside
the first, third and fifth letters of the word Could

parts.note: pi is a ratio, the relationship between a circle's circumference and its diameter

explanation.surface: Wondering whether unlikely people might find romance with a matchmaker's help.
explanation.walkthrough: Pi counts as a 'relationship' because it is the fixed ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter. Read whole, the clue also describes the love god's role.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love shoots arrows that make people fall for each other, so his help secures romances.

clue.text: Timid sort ignoring son's sulky expression

indicators.note: leaving out, so the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a mouse is a timid person
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A shy person snubbing their boy and pulling a face.
explanation.definitionFit: A pout is a sulky pursing of the lips, the facial sense of this French-derived word.

clue.text: In live broadcast term is one unacceptable to many

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go into the word for live

parts.note: to live is to exist

indicators.note: scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A live broadcast in which a phrase used offends many listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live' is the verb, not 'live broadcast'; 'broadcast' scrambles the next word into TREM. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with radical views is beyond the pale for most people, so such a person is unacceptable to many.

clue.text: I will get pole position, for example

parts.note: N is the north pole
a stance is a position

explanation.surface: A racing driver confident of getting pole position on the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole position' suggests motor racing, but the two words split into N and STANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'for instance' means for example, so the noun stands for an example.

clue.text: For starters, sack traffic wardens randomly? It's popular among drivers

indicators.note: the starting letters of the next two words
in no particular order, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A wish to fire traffic wardens at random, which motorists would cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drivers' are golfers, not motorists. Traffic wardens are British officials who issue parking tickets; the Scottish town is the home of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish town is the historic home of golf, a favourite of players who hit drives.

clue.text: Worry about new fellow's dog, for example

indicators.note: around, so the word for worry surrounds the other letters

parts.note: care means worry
Ivor is a man's name, a fellow; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Fretting about the new man's dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivor stands for any fellow, a man's name as crosswords often use. 'dog' is just one example of the definition, signalled by 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat-eating animal is called this, and a dog is one example.

clue.text: Bad hair day set lawyer going, resulting in panic

indicators.note: bad means wrong, so the letters are set wrongly into a new order
departing, so the lawyer's letters leave the mix

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A bad hair day prompts a lawyer to leave in a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' shuffles HAIR DAY SET, and 'going' takes out DA, leaving the eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This word names wild, uncontrolled emotion such as panic or frenzy.

clue.text: A mere 1,000 feet above sea level, perhaps

definitions.text: A mere 1,000 feet above sea level, perhaps

parts.words: A mere 1,000 feet above sea level, perhaps
parts.note: a mere is a lake; this small lake is typically found high up on a mountainside, perhaps a thousand feet up

explanation.surface: Something modestly elevated, only a thousand feet high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mere' looks like 'only', but it is a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mountain lake, so a lake lying well above sea level.

clue.text: On vacation enjoyment is restricted by what may be sole obsession

indicators.note: held within, so the outer letters are hemmed in by the other word

parts.note: a sole is a fish

indicators.note: emptied, so only the outer letters of enjoyment remain

explanation.surface: Holiday fun curtailed by an obsession with footwear soles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' empties 'enjoyment' to ET, which 'is restricted by' FISH. 'Sole' suggests the foot, chiming with 'fetish', but is the flatfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixation or compulsive preoccupation is a synonym for this noun.

clue.text: Act contemptibly? Get lost!

definitions.meaning: to behave like a fool, a tit being a British slang word for an idiot
a rude command to go away

explanation.surface: Two curt remarks one might throw at someone behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense needs the letters respaced as three words, 'be a tit'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang telling someone to leave, and respaced it means to behave like an idiot.

clue.text: Run away from animal, not a tiny one

indicators.note: without, so the tiny creature is removed

parts.note: an antelope is an animal
an ant is a tiny animal

explanation.surface: Fleeing from a large beast, though not a small one.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off secretly, especially to marry, is the meaning of this verb.

clue.text: Without authorisation, left troubled Oklahoma City in US

indicators.note: disturbed, so the remaining letters are mixed up
lacking, so the letters for authorisation and left are taken out

parts.note: an OK is approval or authorisation

explanation.surface: Leaving troubled Oklahoma City without permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oklahoma City' looks like the definition but splits: 'Without' strips out the approval and the left letter, and 'troubled' rearranges what remains, AHOMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A large city in Nebraska, in the American Midwest.

clue.text: Passing criticism as teams cancel

parts.note: sides are teams
to wipe a record is to cancel it

explanation.surface: A sports pundit's dig at teams calling off fixtures.
explanation.definitionFit: A passing, indirect critical remark aimed at someone is called this.

clue.text: Maybe estate agent gutted houses? That's frightening!

indicators.note: contains, so the trimmed word goes round the other
with the insides removed, so the middle letter goes

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
an estate is a type of car, an estate car (US: station wagon)

explanation.surface: An estate agent left devastated by the houses on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Estate agent' reads as one phrase but splits: an estate is a British car type, and 'gutted' leaves SY. 'houses' means contains.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation like 'that's frightening!' is summed up by this adjective, meaning alarming.

clue.text: After second arrest, one makes slow progress

indicators.note: the word for arrest follows the single letter

parts.note: to nail a suspect is to arrest them

explanation.surface: A police officer, after a second arrest, edges slowly ahead in the case.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden mollusc moves notoriously slowly, so it makes slow progress.

clue.text: Single old lady needs one friend, having no life

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, single
nan is British for a grandmother
I is the Roman numeral one
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A lonely elderly woman needs a friend because she has no social life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no life' hints at loneliness but means lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lifeless, like a rock, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: A room and where it's found

parts.note: a loft is a room in the roof

explanation.surface: A description of an attic room and its location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is the room just named: an attic room sits high up in a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means high up, which is where an attic room is located.

clue.text: Fit Liberal into old PM's diary at last

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes into the surname

parts.note: Edward Heath was British Prime Minister 1970-74

indicators.note: the final letter of the word diary

explanation.surface: A Liberal finally fitted into a former Prime Minister's diary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts L inside HEATH, and 'at last' adds Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in good physical shape is the meaning of both words.

clue.text: Having enough to pay for alcohol perhaps

definitions.meaning: alcohol dissolves other substances, so it is an example of a dissolving liquid

explanation.surface: A drinker with enough cash to pay for a round.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means able to pay one's debts, and the noun is a liquid that dissolves things, such as alcohol.
